observation_summary: The method toJavaVersionInt was incorrectly declared to return a float, causing assertion failures when comparing expected integer values (e.g., 0) with the returned float (0.0).
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the method signature from returning a float to returning an int. This is a classic interface/contract mismatch where the caller expected an integer result, but the method signature provided a floating-point type, leading to type-related assertion failures.
evidence_used: The failing test expected an integer (0) but received a float (0.0).
The fix diff shows the method signature changed from 'static float toJavaVersionInt(String version)' to 'static int toJavaVersionInt(String version)'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the return value is a value, the root cause is the method signature contract mismatch, not an incorrect assignment of a variable or constant.
The internal logic of the method was likely correct for calculating the version; the issue was the type contract of the method signature itself.
